patch.value: Recover the historical 2026.10.20 GitHub Release with verified release evidence

The read-only completeness audit reports exactly one missing GitHub Release: v2026.10.20. Its immutable release commit lacks the matching changelog section, so the automatic repair refuses it. The current changelog fix restores main and future release windows, but cannot alter that historical commit. Orchestrator must decide an evidence-preserving recovery path and separately authorize release creation; no tag, npm artifact or GitHub Release was changed here.

value.author: glm-agent
value.text: Root cause diagnosis (worktree at origin/main 089e803): the v2026.10.20 tag, npm 2026.10.20 dist.gitHead and the remote tag all name release commit ee029738 ('Release pm-ops v2026.10.20', authored by github-actions[bot]). That release commit bumped package.json, package-lock.json, manifest.json, index.ts and dist/index.js but did NOT touch CHANGELOG.md: git show v2026.10.20:CHANGELOG.md ends at the 2026.10.15 section - zero sections for 2026.10.20 (and none for 10.16-10.19). git log v2026.10.15..v2026.10.20 -- CHANGELOG.md is empty, so the 2026-10-20 run created its release commit during the changelog generation-drift window (the pending-to-tag drift fixed separately in ops-release-changelog-stability / PR #205, which restored main's changelog afterwards). Current main is healthy: the committed changelog has exactly one section for every one of the 61 release-tag versions, and npm view pm-ops@2026.10.20 dist.gitHead returns the same ee029738. The blocker is therefore NOT current main's changelog but the repair's single note source: repairReleaseCompleteness extracts notes only via git show <release-commit>:CHANGELOG.md, and that immutable commit can never gain a section, so every daily run's --repair refuses forever. Fix plan: keep the release commit's own changelog as the primary note source, and fall back to the audit-time committed changelog (regenerated by changelog:full --all-release-tags and enforced by changelog:check plus a new pre-release section gate) only when the historical commit lacks exactly one section; never read uncommitted working-tree state.

All focused tests pass on the fixed implementation (release-repair.test.ts: 27/27; verify-release-changelog-sections.test.ts: 7/7).

value.text: Review round 1 class audit complete. Only scripts/verify-release-changelog-sections.ts constructed a pre-publication section inventory from tags alone. Generation, full regeneration, equality checks and release notes share scripts/pm-changelog.ts and already pass --release-version-from-package. npm prepublishOnly and both workflow release-check paths delegate to release:check; SDK/CLI ops verify-release delegates to that package command and its JSON/TOON renderers do not recompute versions. Published completeness and repair intentionally audit already-published triples (union of tags/npm/releases), so including an unpublished candidate there would violate the post-publication contract. Packed SDK consumers expose repair, not this repository-only preflight; that code is unchanged. The section verifier now unions normalized historical tags with package.json.version, deduplicates an already-tagged candidate, retains suffix releases, checks first releases, and refuses unusable pending metadata. Explicit inventories work for real non-git trackers; a default unavailable Git scan returns a verifier failure instead of throwing. GitHub inline/review records contain no additional actionable non-blocking findings; Greptile and CodeRabbit notices are unavailable/skipped reviews, not approval. Focused tests: 17 passed, 0 failed/skipped; 64 inventory states plus every required section's missing/duplicate/empty mutations, npm/Bun command execution, prepublish delegation and non-git tracker checks.
